newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex chrmn holds to restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex chrmn holds to restructuring plan.

text.p: Pierre Blayau, chairman of French appliance group Moulinex, said on Friday he would push forward with a controversial restructuring plan to save the company.
"We must clear an operating profit comparable to those of our competitors," Blayau said in a newspaper interview.

"Not only to make financial results but to finance the development of the company, to preserve a high level of industrial employment and keep decision-making centres in France," daily Ouest France quoted him as saying.
But he said the job cuts resulting from the plan could be fewer than originally announced.
Blayau said the amount of time worked in a week would vary by season.

"There will be no typical week. The originality of the idea resides in its seasonality," he said. "When the client wants products, like at Christmas and Mother's Day, we have to be ready. On average during the year I can imagine a 33-hour week but there will be higher weeks and lower weeks."
Blayau said he would maintain salaries at 98 percent of their current levels.
"State aid will allow a reduction in social charges, a reduction which we will redistribute in its entirety to employees through the new work organisation," he said.
Blayau said the plan was a reflection of changing times and the need to adjust to a new environment.

"The job cuts which were set at 2,100 in France and 500 in Germany are principally due to an improvement in productivity in factories and to a better organisation of labour, purchasing and management," he said.
For the fiscal year to March 31 1996, Moulinex reported a net attributable loss of 702 million francs.
